newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Italian U.N. envoy Fulci to lead Security Council.
newsitem.headline: Italian U.N. envoy Fulci to lead Security Council.

text.p: Italian U.N. representative Franceso Paolo Fulci takes over on Sunday as president of the Security Council for the month of December, succeeding ambassador Nugroho Wisnumurti of Indonesia.
Fulci's most pressing task will be to try to ensure the council recommends a candidate for election by the 185-nation General Assembly to the post of U.N. secretary-general.
Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whose re-election for another five year term is opposed by the United States, ends his current term on Dec. 31.
The United States says the United Nations needs new leadership to carry out reforms and vetoed the 74-year-old veteran Egyptian diplomat when the council voted on his candidacy on Nov. 19.

Council members are waiting for the 53-member Organisation of African Unity to come up with a new name or list of names, on the grounds that if Boutros-Ghali cannot win re-election, another African should succeed him.
The presidency of the Security Council rotates monthly according to the English alphabetical order of its 15 member delegations.

Fulci previously presided over the council in September 1995. Italy's two-year term as a non-permanent council member expires at the end of December, as does the membership of Botswana, Germany, Honduras and Indonesia.
